taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

**Given information:**
- Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026
- Submissions close "six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT"
- I need to convert to Madrid time (CET/CEST)

**Finding the deadline date:**
Six days from Saturday, October 24 = Friday, October 30, 2026

**Time conversion:**
- Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time)
- In late October, Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7) or PST (UTC-8) depending on daylight saving
- In 2026, daylight saving time in the US ends on November 1st, so October 30 is still in PDT (UTC-7)
- Madrid in late October uses CET (UTC+1)
- Time difference: CET is 8 hours ahead of PDT

**Calculation:**
11:59 PM PDT (October 30) + 8 hours = 7:59 AM CET (October 31)

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

The contest says the form closes "this coming Monday" from Friday, October 30, 2026.
- That Monday would be November 2, 2026

The deadline is 10:00 AM Los Angeles time on November 2, 2026.

Time zone conversion:
- Los Angeles is in Pacific Time (PT)
- In early November, Los Angeles observes Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is UTC-8
- Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1

The time difference is: UTC+1 minus UTC-8 = 9 hours ahead

So 10:00 AM PST on November 2 = 10:00 + 9 hours = 19:00 (7:00 PM) CET on November 2, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Hackathon End Time Calculation

**Starting point:**
- Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time
- Duration: exactly 48 hours
- Your location: Madrid, Spain

**Calculation:**
- 48 hours from October 24, 2026 at 18:00 = October 26, 2026 at 18:00
- Since you're in Madrid and the time is given in Madrid time, no timezone conversion is needed

**End time:**
The hackathon ends on Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time (which is your local time).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

**Starting point:** October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (Pacific Time)

**Add 72 hours:** 
- 72 hours = 3 days
- October 26, 10:00 AM + 72 hours = October 29, 10:00 AM PT

**Convert PT to Madrid time (CET/CEST):**
- In late October, Spain uses CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1
- Pacific Time in late October is PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7
- The difference is 9 hours (Madrid is 9 hours ahead)
- October 29, 10:00 AM PDT + 9 hours = October 29, 7:00 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me work through this step by step.

**Submissions close:** October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time)

**Results announcement:** 36 hours after submissions close
- 36 hours = 1 day + 12 hours
- October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET + 36 hours = November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET

**Convert ET to Madrid time (CET/CEST):**
In November, Madrid is in CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1, while ET is EST (Eastern Standard Time), which is UTC-5.
- Time difference: CET is 6 hours ahead of EST
- November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET + 6 hours = November 2, 2026 at 5:59 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo time (JST, UTC+9).

First, let me convert this timestamp to a UTC date/time:
- Unix timestamp 1791788340 seconds since January 1, 1970

Dividing by seconds in a year (approximately):
- 1791788340 / 31,536,000 ≈ 56.8 years from 1970
- This puts us around mid-2026

More precisely, 1791788340 seconds from 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC equals:
- 2026-08-27 18:52:20 UTC

Tokyo is UTC+9, so I add 9 hours:
- 2026-08-27 18:52:20 + 9 hours = 2026-08-28 03:52:20 JST

ANSWER: 2026-08-28 03:52

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Deadline Conversion to Madrid Time

The deadline is given in UTC (Z = Zulu time = UTC+0).

Madrid is in the Central European Time zone:
- **CEST** (Central European Summer Time) = UTC+2 (late March to late October)
- **CET** (Central European Winter Time) = UTC+1 (late October to late March)

The date 2026-10-25 falls in late October. Madrid switches from CEST to CET on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, that switch occurs on October 25th at 3:00 AM CEST (which becomes 2:00 AM CET).

The deadline at 02:30:00 UTC occurs **before** the clock change at 03:00 CEST, so Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

Converting: 02:30 UTC + 2 hours = 04:30 CEST

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026 and convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid time.

**Finding the last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026 has 31 days. Let me work backwards:
- October 31, 2026 is a Saturday
- October 30, 2026 is a Friday
- October 25, 2026 is a Sunday

So the last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.

**Converting 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid time:**
- Pacific Time on October 25, 2026 would be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time, UTC-7)
- Madrid is in CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2) in late October... actually, let me check: daylight saving time in Europe ends on the last Sunday of October. So on October 25, Madrid would still be in CEST (UTC+2).
- The time difference: UTC+2 minus UTC-7 = 9 hours ahead

11:59 PM (23:59) PDT + 9 hours = 08:59 (next day, October 26)

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026, then convert that to Lima time.

In the US, daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, that's November 1st.

The deadline is 12:00 noon EST (Eastern Standard Time) on November 1, 2026.

Now I need to convert this to Lima time:
- Lima is in the Peru Standard Time zone (PET), which is UTC-5
- Eastern Standard Time (EST) is UTC-5
- Wait, that means they're the same! But let me reconsider...

Actually, when the US "ends daylight saving time," they're switching from EDT (Eastern Daylight Time, UTC-4) to EST (Eastern Standard Time, UTC-5).

On November 1, 2026, at 12:00 noon, the US will be in EST (UTC-5).
Lima is in PET (UTC-5) year-round.

Since both are UTC-5 at that moment, 12:00 noon EST = 12:00 noon PET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" to Tokyo time (JST).

First, let me clarify the time:
- 24:00 on December 31 is equivalent to 00:00 on January 1
- So this is January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12, which represents the last timezone on Earth. This is the latest possible moment for a deadline.

Converting from AoE (UTC-12) to JST (UTC+9):
- The difference is 9 - (-12) = 21 hours
- January 1, 2027, 00:00 AoE + 21 hours = January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 to New York time (since you'll be in New York that week).

Let me work through the time zones:
- Sydney (AEDT - Australian Eastern Daylight Time) in October is UTC+11
- New York (EDT - Eastern Daylight Time) in October is UTC-4

The difference is 15 hours, with Sydney ahead.

5:00 PM (17:00) on October 5 in Sydney = 17:00 AEDT
Converting to UTC: 17:00 - 11 hours = 06:00 UTC on October 5
Converting to EDT: 06:00 - 4 hours = 02:00 EDT on October 5

So the deadline is 2:00 AM on October 5, 2026 in New York time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
